title: Eventual equality of differential ranks under a finite field extension
statement: Let $p$ be prime, let $K$ be a field of characteristic $p$, and let $L/K$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $(K_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$ be a nonempty family of subfields of $K$ such that $[K:K_\alpha]<\infty$ for every $\alpha$, $\bigcap_{\alpha\in I}K_\alpha=K^p=\{x^p:x\in K\}$, and for every $\alpha,\beta\in I$ some $\gamma\in I$ satisfies $K_\gamma\subseteq K_\alpha\cap K_\beta$. Then there exists $\beta\in I$ such that for every subfield $K\prime\subseteq K_\beta$ with $[K:K\prime]<\infty$, one has $\dim_L\Omega_{L/K\prime}=\dim_K\Omega_{K/K\prime}$, where $\Omega$ denotes Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials].

source.place: Expose IV Proposition 1.2.4 (Matsumura stabilization), printed p.49; proof using IV 1.2.1–1.2.3, printed pp.48–49.

proof.text: Set $n=[L:K]$. Choose a $K$-basis $(e_i)_{1\leq i\leq n}$ of $L$ using [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-free] and finite-dimensionality; $n\geq1$ since $1\ne0$ in $L$. Put $b_i=e_i^p$. These vectors are independent over $K^p$: if $\sum_i c_i b_i=0$ with $c_i\in K^p$, choose $a_i\in K$ with $a_i^p=c_i$. In characteristic $p$ this is $(\sum_i a_i e_i)^p=0$. Injectivity of Frobenius in the field $L$ gives $\sum_i a_i e_i=0$, and the basis gives $a_i=0$, hence $c_i=0$, for every $i$.

source.place: Tag 09FN, lemma-vector-space-is-free; Frobenius calculation written out here.

proof.text: Consider the $K$-linear subspace $V=\{(c_i)\in K^n:\sum_i c_i b_i=0\}$ of $K^n$, viewing $L$ as a $K$-vector space. Step 1 says $V\cap(K^p)^n=0$. Every $K_\alpha$ contains $K^p$ by the intersection hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-intersection-subfields-subspace] with ambient field $K$, base subfield $K^p$ and this $V$. The required index set is nonempty, $n\geq1$, the intersection is $K^p$, and downward directedness is assumed. Its contrapositive supplies $\beta$ such that $V\cap K_\beta^n=0$. Thus the $b_i$ are independent over $K_\beta$, and hence over every subfield of $K_\beta$.

source.place: Tag 07P3, lemma-intersection-subfields-subspace; applied to the relation subspace of the Frobenius powers of a basis. Compare ILO IV 1.2.1.

proof.text: Fix any $K'\subseteq K_\beta$ with $[K:K']<\infty$. Inside $K$ let $E=K'K^p$, the subfield generated by $K'$ and $K^p$; inside $L$ let $F=K'L^p$. Then $E\subseteq K_\beta$ and $F=EL^p$, because $K^p\subseteq L^p$. A $K'$-derivation $D$ on $K$ kills $x^p$ since $D(x^p)=px^{p-1}D(x)=0$. Its kernel is a subfield: the Leibniz rule gives $D(x^{-1})=-x^{-2}D(x)$ for $x\ne0$. It therefore kills $E$. Conversely an $E$-derivation kills $K'$. The identical argument in $L$ replaces $K'$ by $F$. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] now gives inverse maps, each carrying $\mathrm dx$ to $\mathrm dx$, and therefore $\Omega_{K/K'}\cong\Omega_{K/E}$ and $\Omega_{L/K'}\cong\Omega_{L/F}$.

source.place: Tag 07P2, lemma-p-basis, proof: every derivation annihilates the compositum with pth powers; ILO IV 1.2.4, first proof paragraph.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-frobenius-basis-compositum] to the original finite $K$-basis $(e_i)$ and $S=E$, which is a subfield of $K$ containing $K^p$. It says that $F=EL^p$ is exactly the $E$-span of the $b_i$. Step 2, since $E\subseteq K_\beta$, gives independence over $E$. Consequently $(b_i)$ is an $E$-basis of $F$ and $[F:E]=n$.

source.place: Tag 07P4, lemma-intersection-subfields, proof of (2), coefficient expansions; use the arbitrary-basis formulation of the cited node.

proof.text: The finite $K'$-spanning family for $K$ also spans it over $E$, so $[K:E]$ is finite. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] to $E\subseteq K\subseteq L$: $[L:E]=n[K:E]<\infty$. Since $F$ is an intermediate field of $L/E$, any $E$-spanning family of $L$ spans it over $F$ as well, so $[L:F]<\infty$. Apply the same node to $E\subseteq F\subseteq L$, obtaining $[L:E]=[L:F][F:E]=[L:F]n$. Cancellation of the positive integer $n$ gives $[L:F]=[K:E]$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-p-independent-extends-to-p-basis] to the empty family for $K/E$ and for $L/F$. The empty family is $p$-independent since its only monomial is $1$. This gives relative $p$-bases indexed by sets $A$ and $B$. Since $K^p\subseteq E$ and $L^p\subseteq F$, their bounded monomials are bases over $E$ and $F$, respectively. Both index sets are finite: the individual basis elements are a subfamily of the monomial bases (use exponent $1$ at a single index), so are independent in finite-dimensional vector spaces. Write $r=|A|$ and $s=|B|$. There are exactly $p^r$ and $p^s$ bounded monomials, giving $[K:E]=p^r$ and $[L:F]=p^s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-differentials-basis], their differentials form bases of $\Omega_{K/E}$ and $\Omega_{L/F}$, of dimensions $r$ and $s$. Step 5 gives $p^r=p^s$. Since $p\geq2$, integer powers of $p$ strictly increase, whence $r=s$. Step 3 yields $\dim_L\Omega_{L/K'}=s=r=\dim_K\Omega_{K/K'}$. The choice of $\beta$ was independent of $K'$, as required.

tool_uses.why: A finite field extension has a vector-space basis; this is generic field linear algebra, not a replacement for the perverse-duality route.

The descending-intersection criterion detects a nonzero coefficient relation in K^n; this is exactly the generic linear-algebra input ILO IV 1.2.1 used in stabilization, and the unit has no such statement.
The arbitrary-basis coefficient description of L^p E is needed to turn stabilized independence into [L^p E:E]=[L:K]; the unit has no field-compositum formula.
The generic tower law compares degrees over E in the two intermediate-field towers; the unit has no degree-multiplicativity statement.
The relative p-basis existence clause is used on empty independent families, for the two finite exponent-one extensions. The unit has no p-basis construction.
The relative p-basis differential characterization turns the two equal degrees into equal differential dimensions; no node of the perverse unit supplies this commutative-algebra fact.

Source: ILO IV Prop. 1.2.4 (printed p.49), with 1.2.1–1.2.3 on pp.48–49, read in full. The item statement matches it hypothesis by hypothesis. 'Nonempty family' is added, and it is needed: an empty family over a perfect K makes ∃β false. The quantifier over all cofinite K' ⊆ K_β is kept, including K' that do not contain K^p. The proof is the agent's own direct route, recorded as proof_origin.by=agent, and every step holds. Step 1: the e_i^p are independent over K^p, by injectivity of Frobenius; this needs no separability. Step 2: the contrapositive of the 07P3 node is applied to the relation space V ⊆ K^n with k=K^p, and all of that node's hypotheses hold (nonempty index set, n≥1, directed family). Step 3 is correctly marked elementary: since derivations kill E=K'K^p and F=K'L^p, Ω_{K/K'}≅Ω_{K/E} and Ω_{L/K'}≅Ω_{L/F}. Step 4: the frobenius-basis-compositum node is applied with S=E; it gives spanning only, and independence comes from Step 2, so [F:E]=n. Step 5: the tower law is applied to both towers with finiteness checked, then n>0 is cancelled. Step 6: the relative p-basis existence and differential-basis nodes are applied with k=E and k=F, using kK^p=E. The index sets are finite, p^r=p^s gives r=s, and Step 3 transfers the result to K'. Each cited statement says what its step takes from it. There are no new nodes and no cycle (the proof_deps closure of 23 nodes does not contain the item). There is no duplicate: the related pbc node intersection-subfields-differentials-powers is ILO 1.2.3, a different statement. All six declared tool_uses are generic sk-thm-p1 field-theory tools used as black boxes, and I accept them. No SGA source is cited. tools/review_split.py on the snapshot gives PASS. Small cases checked: L=K; F_p(t) with L=K(t^{1/p}) and K'=F_p(t^{p^2}); and F_p(s,t) with L=K(s^{1/p}), where the exceptional indices are exactly those with s∈K_α.
